summary: Yahweh sends his word and ice melts into running water. The same verb describes what tears do to a couch in a night of weeping and what a frightening report does to the courage of those who hear it.

senses.definition: What was solid gives way. When Yahweh sends his word after the frost, water flows. The psalmist pictures a whole couch dissolving in his tears.

evidence.note: The other half of the line pictures the bed swimming every night.
Under rebuke, what a person prizes wastes away.

senses.definition: Caleb says that the other spies melted the people's heart. The people heard of the fortified cities and refused to go up.

evidence.note: The woman wets Jesus' feet with her tears.

words.summary: The word occurs in instructions for guarding the palace. The precise duty and any connection with melting are unclear.

senses.definition: One of the companies is stationed at the gate behind the runners to keep watch over the house. This word qualifies that charge.

words.summary: The Peshitta uses the verb for the swelling expected after a snakebite. How this sense relates to melting is unclear.

senses.definition: After the viper fastens on Paul's hand, the islanders expect his body to swell or for him to fall down dead.

evidence.locator: s.v. ܡܣܐ, peal and aphel, pp. 283–284
evidence.note: Includes a melting heart, dissolving or washing away, and wetting with tears. The entry also gives thickening or curdling.

note: The Hebrew noun מַסָּח is attested once. A connection with נסח has also been proposed, but the palace instructions give too little detail to decide. The zero-token m.cq.ad and n.dt.ab are cross-references. SEDRA lexeme 1814 gives the Peshitta's distinct sense at Acts 28:6. The place Massah is named for putting Yahweh to the test in Exodus 17:7 and belongs with נסה.
